meta.name: Lunora Astro Rules
meta.purpose: Central rulebook that scores normalized activity tags against daily astrological conditions and ranks the activity catalog accordingly.
meta.important_note: Numeric weights are Lunora-specific product-model implementation weights derived from the stated astrological framework. They are not scientific measurements, empirical effect sizes, or universal astrology standards.

reserved_future_vocabulary.note: These concepts are reserved for future use because the current normalized activity catalog does not use them as active tags. They must not be used as modifier targets until they are added to the activity catalog and supported by the scoring rules.

source_term_normalization.practice: Do not map 'practice' by word alone. Map the actual behavior: physical practice -> exercise and/or movement; meditative or breath-based practice -> mindfulness and, when applicable, rest; skill practice -> focus and/or continue. Use start_new only when the activity genuinely begins a new practice.
source_term_normalization.workout: Map workout to exercise. Add movement only when the activity itself is meaningfully movement-based; do not automatically assign both tags.
source_term_normalization.challenge: Map by the actual structure of the challenge: start_new when beginning a new challenge; commit when it creates an ongoing commitment; plan when the challenge is being designed; continue when an existing challenge is being resumed or continued. Add exercise and/or movement only when the challenge is physical.
source_term_normalization.self_care: Map by actual behavior: beauty_care for grooming or cosmetic care; rest for deliberate recovery; mindfulness for attention-based calming practices. Add other action tags only when the activity explicitly contains those behaviors.
source_term_normalization.release: Do not use release as a generic action. Map it to review, organize, set_boundary, reflect, clarify, or another existing canonical action only when that behavior is explicitly present in the activity.
source_term_normalization.complete: Reserved. Do not emit complete as an active action until the activity catalog contains the tag and the scoring rules explicitly support it.

suppression_semantics.arithmetic_behavior: Do not add -4 to tag scores or to the final astro-fit score.
suppression_semantics.eligibility_behavior: A matched -4 conditional activity modifier marks the activity as ineligible for recommendation.
suppression_semantics.score_behavior: The astro-fit score may still be calculated for diagnostics, but eligibility is false.
suppression_semantics.scope: Use -4 only for explicit activity-level suppression rules, never as a normal tag modifier.

aggregation.tag_score_rule: For every canonical tag actually carried by the activity, start at base_score 5, add all applicable modifiers, apply the relevant category caps, then clamp that tag score to 0..10.

conditional_activity_modifier_policy.application_stage: Apply after the weighted tag-based astro-fit score is calculated.
conditional_activity_modifier_policy.non_suppressive_values: Add matched conditional activity modifiers other than -4 to the activity-level astro-fit score, subject to conditional_activity_modifier_total_cap.
conditional_activity_modifier_policy.multiple_suppressors: One matched -4 is sufficient to make the activity ineligible. Preserve every matched suppressing rule ID as a diagnostic reason.
conditional_activity_modifier_policy.hard_block_allowed_false_scope: hard_block_allowed=false prevents that specific rule or conditional branch from hard-suppressing the activity. It does not cancel an independent suppressor from another rule.

low.rule: Do not hide a low-intensity activity solely because a critical action is neutral or mildly discouraged. Explicit -4 suppression still applies.

medium.rule: Every critical action carried by a medium-intensity activity must score at least 4. A score of 3 or lower makes the activity ineligible.

high.rule: Every critical action carried by a high-intensity activity must score at least 6. High-stakes critical actions should be actively supported rather than merely neutral.

noncritical_action_policy.rule: Noncritical action tags contribute to ranking through their mean score and do not individually veto an activity. Suppression can still occur through explicit -4 rules, relationship-mode gates, or intensity rules based on converging strong primary negatives.

strong_negative_policy.qualifies_when: A primary rule directly applies a modifier of -2 or lower to at least one action or required relationship_mode carried by the activity, or a matched conditional activity rule applies an activity_modifier of -2 or lower.
does_not_qualify: a replaced rule that has been deduplicated
a rule branch whose hard_block_allowed value is false
strong_negative_policy.duplicate_modifier_behavior: Multiple -2 modifiers produced by the same primary rule count as one strong negative signal, not multiple signals.
strong_negative_policy.relevance_requirement: A strong negative signal counts only when it actually touches the activity through one of its actions, required relationship_modes, or a matched conditional activity rule.

low.rule: Relationship-mode scores affect ranking only. Do not hide a low-intensity relationship activity unless an explicit -4 suppression rule independently applies.

medium.rule: Hide the activity when any required relationship_mode scores 3 or lower and at least one relevant strong primary negative signal applies to the activity.

high.rule: Hide the activity when any required relationship_mode scores 4 or lower and at least one relevant strong primary negative signal applies to the activity.

low.rule: Low-risk everyday activities are ranking-first. Do not hard-suppress them because of ordinary negative scoring or converging strong negatives. Suppress only when a matched rule explicitly produces -4 and does not prohibit hard blocking.

medium.rule: Suppress on an explicit -4, when two or more distinct relevant strong primary negative rules converge on the activity, or when a medium-intensity critical action fails its minimum-score gate.

high.rule: Suppress on an explicit -4, when two or more distinct relevant strong primary negative rules converge on the activity, when a high-intensity critical action fails its minimum-score gate, or when the high-intensity relationship-mode gate fails.

ranking_formula.relationship_formula_applies_when: Use the relationship formula when relationship_modes is non-empty.
ranking_formula.dimension_score_rule: The score of each dimension is the arithmetic mean of the final scores of the activity tags present in that dimension.
ranking_formula.missing_dimension_policy: If an activity contains no tags for a weighted dimension, omit that dimension rather than assigning an artificial neutral score, then proportionally renormalize the remaining dimension weights to sum to 1.

non_astrological_tie_breakers.rule: Apply recommendation-system tie-breakers only after astrological eligibility and astro-fit scoring. They must not alter the meaning of the astrological score.

output_contract.astro_fit_score: Number from 0 to 10 after clamping and rounding.
output_contract.eligible: Boolean indicating whether the activity may be recommended.
output_contract.suppression_reasons: Array of matched rule IDs that caused hard suppression or a failed gate.
output_contract.strong_negative_rule_ids: Distinct relevant primary rule IDs counted as strong negative signals.

deferred_rules.reason: Generic house-number-only scoring is astrologically under-specified. A transit house has meaning only after the transiting planet, the reference chart and the house system are known. Do not activate transit_house_1 through transit_house_12 as standalone activity modifiers.

reference_chart_policy.event_chart: Do not mix event-chart houses into personalized natal transit-house scoring.
reference_chart_policy.moon_chart: Do not use as a substitute for natal houses.
reference_chart_policy.unknown_birth_time: Do not calculate natal transit-house rules when house cusps cannot be determined reliably.

implementation_direction: Build planet-by-house routing rather than generic house-only bonuses.
Combine the natural significations of the transiting planet with the topics of the natal house.
Keep house effects secondary unless a future personalized electional model explicitly justifies stronger weighting.
Do not create hard suppression from house placement alone.
Do not use the modern sign-equals-house alphabet as a substitute for actual house significations.
deferred_rules.example: transiting Venus in the user's natal 5th house and transiting Saturn in the user's natal 5th house must not produce the same activity modifiers.

deferred_rules.reason: North Node and South Node must not be translated into generic 'future/growth' versus 'past/reconnection' activity bonuses. Their effect depends on the contacted planet or significator and on the exact contact geometry.
implementation_direction: Do not restore generic north_node_contact -> start_new/personal_growth bonuses.
Do not restore generic south_node_contact -> past/reconnection bonuses.
Review conjunctions to the Nodes first before considering other aspect geometries.
Model the Node as modifying the contacted significator rather than as an independent activity-topic generator.

deferred_rules.reason: A conjunction cannot be classified globally as supportive or hard. Its expression depends strongly on the nature and condition of the planets involved, so conjunctions require pair-by-pair rules.
implementation_direction: Do not automatically copy trine/sextile modifiers onto conjunctions.
Do not automatically copy square/opposition modifiers onto conjunctions.
Audit each planet pair separately.
Respect astronomical feasibility when defining aspect types for each planet pair.
Sun-Mercury and Sun-Venus relationships require special solar-proximity handling because their possible geocentric configurations are constrained.

deferred_rules.reason: Retrogradation is a traditional planetary debility for Jupiter and Saturn, but these slow retrograde periods persist for long spans. A generic daily penalty may flatten recommendation scores for months unless relevance and weighting are carefully constrained.
implementation_direction: If activated, prefer a small planet-profile-specific friction rather than generic activity penalties.
Do not create generic past, review or reconnect bonuses merely because the planet is retrograde.
Do not allow long retrograde periods to dominate the daily recommendation engine.

deferred_rules.reason: Uranus, Neptune and Pluto retrogrades belong to modern astrology rather than the traditional planetary-condition framework used for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn. Their long duration also makes them weak candidates for generic daily ranking modifiers.
implementation_direction: Do not activate Uranus, Neptune or Pluto retrograde as generic daily modifiers by default.
Prefer using their exact aspects and other time-specific contacts, which provide greater daily discrimination.
If they are ever activated, keep effects small and restricted to directly relevant planet-profile tags.

deferred_rules.reason: The active eclipse rules refer to configured_eclipse_window, but no universal evidence-based or universally accepted electional number of surrounding days exists. An arbitrary three-day, seven-day or similar window must not be invented inside the scoring rules.
implementation_direction: Keep solar and lunar eclipse windows configurable outside individual rule definitions.
Use the same configured value consistently throughout the engine.
Do not silently expand the eclipse influence period from social-media conventions.
Solar eclipse must continue to replace new_moon during overlap.
Lunar eclipse must continue to replace full_moon during overlap.

deferred_rules.reason: The Moon's traditional essential dignity is technically distinct from moon-sign activity routing. Cancer domicile, Taurus exaltation, Scorpio fall and Capricorn detriment must not be hidden inside generic activity-topic bonuses or penalties.
implementation_direction: Keep moon_taurus and moon_cancer activity bonuses separate from essential dignity.
Do not automatically punish Scorpio or Capricorn activities because the Moon is debilitated there.
If activated, treat dignity as a condition of the Moon itself rather than as evidence that particular topics are inherently good or bad.

deferred_rules.reason: Under-the-beams is technically distinct from both combustion and cazimi and should not be collapsed into either condition.
implementation_direction: Cazimi must remain mutually exclusive with combustion.
Under-the-beams must remain distinct from combustion.
Do not apply generic solar-proximity status rules to Uranus, Neptune or Pluto without a separate modern policy.
Handle lunar solar proximity through the lunar-condition model rather than duplicating generic planet-status scoring.

deferred_rules.reason: The active aspect rules specify aspect type but do not yet define a single global production standard for orb, exactness and applying versus separating status. Without this, the same sky can produce different recommendation results depending on the upstream astrology calculator.
implementation_direction: Use one centralized aspect calculator for every active aspect rule.
Do not allow individual rules to invent their own hidden orb conventions.
Store the underlying aspect event ID so identical astronomical events can be deduplicated.
Applying, exact and separating contacts must be distinguishable in sky data even if the first production version ultimately gives them equal scoring.
Validate impossible geocentric aspect combinations before a rule can enter production.
